title: Circadian Clock Gating of Plastidic Nitrate Reductase (NR) Activity under Photoperiod Extension
description: Doctoral research detailing circadian clock components (CCA1/LHY) gating Nitrate Reductase (NR, EC 1.7.1.1) phosphorylation under 20-hour extended photoperiod regimes.
image_caption: Bioluminescence reporter assay tracking CIRCADIAN AND CLOCK ASSOCIATED 1 (CCA1) promoter activity.
overview: Nitrate Reductase (NR, EC 1.7.1.1) catalyzes the rate-limiting step of nitrate reduction in plant cytosol. NR enzyme activity undergoes strict circadian regulation, peaking 2 hours after subjective dawn driven by CCA1/LHY transcription factors. This paper establishes that extending photoperiod beyond 18 hours disrupts circadian gating, causing 14-3-3 protein phosphorylation and inactivation of NR. Maintaining a 16h/8h light-dark cycle optimizes NR Vmax (4.2 µmol NO2⁻/g FW/h), suppressing residual tissue nitrate accumulation below EU safety thresholds (< 2,500 mg/kg).

climate_strategy.strategy: Set photoperiod strictly to 16 hours ON / 8 hours OFF. Align fertigation pulse delivery to coincide with peak morning NR activity (ZT2-ZT6) when cytosolic NADH availability is maximal.

crop_steering.intro: Photoperiodic and enzymatic alignment steering matrix.

fertigation.intro: Dosing alignment with diurnal enzymatic reduction cycles.
fertigation.vegetative_phase: Deliver 70% of daily Calcium Nitrate [PubChem CID 24963] during ZT0 to ZT6 to match peak NR enzymatic activity.
fertigation.generative_phase: Flush root zone with pure water 48 hours prior to harvest to deplete vacuolar NO3⁻ pools.
